parameter_source: Drone: Sacramento et al. 2019 (50 mph / 80 km/h, 30-min endurance, 5 kg payload); Robot: Starship Gen 3 (6 km/h, 10 kg payload, ~6.4 km delivery radius) and Ostermeier 2021 (5 km/h robot, 8 robots per truck); Costs: Malik et al., VRP-DR, arXiv:2505.23584, Table 3

parameter_sources.truck_speed: Urban delivery truck cruise speed, literature standard (35-45 km/h).
parameter_sources.drone_speed: Sacramento et al. 2019: 50 mph (80 km/h) delivery drone.
parameter_sources.robot_speed: Starship Gen 3 delivery robot: 6 km/h max.
parameter_sources.Q_d: Sacramento et al. 2019: 5 kg drone payload.
parameter_sources.E_d: 30-min endurance at 80 km/h => 40 km max sortie distance (Sacramento et al. 2019).
parameter_sources.E_r: Starship ~6.4 km delivery radius => ~12 km max sortie distance at 6 km/h (~2 h).
parameter_sources.T_max: Per-instance depot close time from the raw TDRP-TW file (index 0 of the close-time vector), so the route-duration limit equals the instance horizon instead of a flat 10 h.

T_max_source: depot close time from raw file 17-25.txt (replaces raw header T_max=10.0)
robot_fleet_assumption: Robot fleet parameters are stored separately. Current robot values are experimental placeholders because robot-specific benchmark data is unavailable.
assumptions: Canonical end depot n+1 duplicates raw depot 0.
Robot layer uses the same benchmark distance matrix because TDRP-TW coordinates are unavailable.
Realistic v1 hardware parameters applied (see parameter_sources): drone 80 km/h / 5 kg / 40 km sortie, robot 6 km/h / 10 kg / 12 km sortie.
T_max is the per-instance depot close time, so route-duration penalties only trigger on genuine horizon violations.
warnings: This is a truck-drone benchmark converted to a truck-drone-robot experiment.
Robot movement is a benchmark-distance surrogate, not a sidewalk-network shortest path. Use scripts/build_real_world_instance.py for OSM pedestrian-network robot data.
